title: Cal Newport's Cure for 'Pseudo-Productivity'
alt_title_1: Why Looking Busy at Work Destroys Your Real Output
description_hook: Instant Slack replies and packed Zoom calendars make you look hardworking while starving your most valuable projects. Here is computer scientist Cal Newport's 3-part cure for Pseudo-Productivity.

scenes.headline: Why Instant Replies Ruin Real Output
scenes.stat_label: CHAT REPLIES THAT FRAGMENT YOUR BEST THINKING
bullets: Visible busyness feels safe in the moment
Yet frantic motion starves long-term career assets
scenes.narration: Answering Slack messages in thirty seconds feels productive. Computer scientist Cal Newport argues this habit of constant motion crowds out your best work.

scenes.headline: The Rise of Pseudo-Productivity
bullets: Knowledge work lacks a visible factory conveyor belt
Offices mistook inbox speed and meetings for real value
scenes.narration: In his book Slow Productivity, Newport diagnoses modern knowledge work with pseudo-productivity: using visible busyness, packed calendars, and instant replies as a stand-in for useful results.

scenes.headline: Context Switching Taxes Every Project
scenes.left_body: 7 active projects + nonstop pings -> chronic burnout
scenes.right_body: 2 capped priorities + quiet blocks -> flagship mastery
scenes.narration: Every time you juggle seven active projects and thirty chat threads, context-switching taxes your brain until nothing meaningful ever crosses the finish line.

scenes.headline: Cal Newport's 3-Part Operating Shift
scenes.stat_subtext: Do fewer things • Work at a natural pace • Obsess over quality
scenes.narration: Newport's cure has three rules: cap major active projects at two, work at a sustainable seasonal pace, and obsess over undeniable craft quality.

scenes.headline: Ship Artifacts, Not Inbox Speed
scenes.stat_label: HARD CAP ON ACTIVE MAJOR GOALS
bullets: Batch messages twice daily instead of reacting all day
Judge weeks by finished craft, never hours online
scenes.narration: Five years from now, nobody will remember how quickly you cleared your inbox, they will only remember the flagship assets you actually finished.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
